varint.pext_crossover_bytes.source: host kit corpus rows (inputs 1, 2, 5, 9 bytes, isolated calls), the kit rule (smallest length where pext SWAR beats unrolled by >= 2 %), per run: [5, 5, 5, 5, 5]. UNCERTAIN: the harnesses disagree. zchar run6 (streaming decode of 4096 varints; pext/scalar cycle ratio 4: 1.36, 5: 1.11, 9: 0.20, 10: 0.29) has pext slower at 5 bytes in the final build (earlier builds: run6/kernel-tables.md ranges), and no 6-8-byte rows, so from run6 alone the crossover lies between 5 and 9 bytes. The 9-10-byte zchar win is the decoder's over-8-byte fallback (constant 8-byte advance, predictable tail loop), not pext; the kit SWAR falls back to the generic loop there (unrolled/SWAR at 9 bytes: 1.00). Follow-up with 1-10-byte inputs (host-results/avx512-characterize/followup): kit rule per run [4, 4, 4, 4, 4] (isolated calls); zchar streaming per pass [5, 5, 6, 5]; lengths where pext wins by >= 2 % in every run of both harnesses: [6, 7, 8] (docs/avx512-zen5.md §6.7)

varint.pext_crossover_bytes.isolated_cal.source: follow-up: host kit corpus `qmdb` with its varint inputs extended to 1-10 bytes (patched copy, kernels unchanged; isolated calls on one buffer), the kit rule per run: [4, 4, 4, 4, 4]; median unrolled/SWAR ratio by length: 1: 0.89, 2: 0.94, 3: 0.99, 4: 1.05, 5: 1.10, 6: 1.16, 7: 1.24, 8: 1.31, 9: 0.99, 10: 0.96 (> 1: pext faster; at 9-10 bytes the SWAR falls back to the generic loop) (docs/avx512-zen5.md §6.7)

varint.pext_crossover_bytes.streaming.source: follow-up: zchar `kernels bits` (streaming decode of 4096 fixed-length varints, 1-10 bytes), per pass (bits-1.jsonl, bits-2.jsonl, bits-3.jsonl, bits-core10.jsonl): [5, 5, 6, 5], i.e. the smallest length from which pext beats the scalar decoder by >= 2 % at every length up to 8; pext/scalar cycle ratio over the passes by length: 1: 2.56-2.56, 2: 1.70-1.70, 3: 1.29-1.71, 4: 1.02-1.37, 5: 0.86-1.11, 6: 0.73-0.93, 7: 0.64-0.80, 8: 0.67-0.95, 9: 0.17-0.20, 10: 0.24-0.28; run6 build at 5 bytes: 1.11. The scalar decoder is layout-sensitive; 9-10 bytes use the pext decoder's over-8-byte fallback (docs/avx512-zen5.md §6.7)
